name: NUCLEO-U083RC (ST Nucleo-64 board, MB1932)
sources: STM32U083xC datasheet DS14463 Rev 2 (features, ST's CoreMark and current figures); Nucleo-64 MB1932 user manual UM3256 Rev 2 (jumpers JP1, JP4, JP5, JP6 to JP10, Tables 7, 9 and 10, Figure 3 top layout); both read on st.com 2026-10-07

columns.head: The chip: STM32U083RC
items: Runs the program, up to 56 million steps a second (56 MHz). A 1 kB cache hides flash wait states
Holds the program. Kept when the power is off
Working memory, all of it parity-checked
The chip accepts 1.71 to 3.6 V. ST's low-power line: 52 µA per MHz running, 16 nA asleep in Shutdown (ST's figures)

columns.head: Connections inside the chip
items: Serial text. USART2 goes to the Mac through the debug probe; USART1 is on Arduino D8 and D2
Two-wire sensor bus / fast bus for displays and memory chips
Measures a voltage in 4,096 steps, and makes one, so the chip can test itself with a wire
Encrypts in hardware. The reason this board is here
Full-speed USB with no crystal; drives a segment display directly

columns.head: On the board, and missing
items: STLINK-V2EC debug probe on USB-C, green LED LD4, blue button B1, reset button B2, 32.768 kHz crystal
ARDUINO Uno V3 sockets plus two rows of ST morpho pins that reach every chip pin
No FPU, no math accelerator, no radio
ST says keep readout protection off on this probe: with it on, the program stops running
